text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

## Abstract
GSE309890 investigates how the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) sertraline influences antibiotic resistance in *Escherichia coli* by stress-driven shifts in the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP). The study highlights potential metabolic interventions to reverse resistance and protect millions of SSRI users. It uses high-throughput sequencing to profile *E. coli* samples from adaptive evolution experiments. Supplementary data includes one downloadable file containing processed expression values.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** The study focuses on the unintended risk of antibiotic resistance associated with SSRIs, uncovering a compensatory mechanism involving the PPP and Complex I in *E. coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655*.

**Literature Review.** No PubMed record is linked to the study, indicating it may be unpublished or not yet indexed.

**Knowledge Gap.** Previously, the metabolic traits behind SSRI-induced resistance were not well-characterized.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The study aimed to identify reversible metabolic pathways linked to SSRI-induced antibiotic resistance, hypothesizing that targeting the PPP could restore susceptibility.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** GEO Series analysis with high-throughput sequencing profiling six *E. coli* samples subjected to adaptive evolution and control conditions. 

**Materials.** GEO Series accession: GSE309890. FTP directory URL: [GEO FTP tree](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/).

**Procedures.** Metadata and supplementary files retrieved. Supplementary directory inspected for processed data availability.

**Statistical Analysis.** Coverage validation included FTP file size (510K) and modification date.

## III. Results
**Data Presentation.**

| File Name                            | URL                                                                 | File Size | Last Modified         |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------------------|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz    | [Download](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz) | 510K      | 2025-11-14 11:10     |

**Findings.** The supplementary directory hosts one file containing FPKM (Fragments Per Kilobase of transcript per Million mapped reads) data for all samples.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The availability of CSV-format FPKM values facilitates in-depth resistance profiling and transcriptional analysis.

**Context.** The study summary connects SSRI-induced resistance with redox stress mechanisms in *E. coli*, suggesting novel targets for therapeutic interventions.

**Limitations.** Lack of linked PubMed records and minimal supplementary files limit immediate use beyond provided FPKM data.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** The study provides valuable insights into SSRI-induced antibiotic resistance. Future work should include additional datasets and publication indexing.

Data provided by NCBI GEO and retrieved using the GEO API.
